This includes solving one equation (with multiple variables) for one unknown, substituting this solution into the other equation, solving that equation (with only one variable) and finally substituting this number back into the first solution to find the full result.
Sometimes we have multiple equations with multiple variables. How does that work? And how can we solve all equations together?

Suppose that we go to the market to buy fruit. First we get eight apples and six bananas for nine euros. Later on, realizing we actually need more, we go back and get another two apples and five bananas, this time paying four euros. Based on this info, can we determine how much individual apples and bananas cost?

The story above can be translated into equations. Let's call the price of an apple and the price of a banana . Similarly, we can turn our second fruit stall visit into an equation too, giving Our goal now is to find a combination of values for and that satisfies all of the given equations. We call such a set of equations a system of equations and the combination of values for the variables that matches all equations is known as the solution of the system. Finding it is known as solving the system of equations.

There are various ways to solve a system of equations. We will use one of the most generally applicable methods. We first pick one equation (usually the easiest) and solve it for one variable.
